title: Biextensions of commutative group schemes in invertible modules
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme] and let $P,Q$ be commutative group objects in schemes over $S$, with the group laws of [def-sc-group-scheme]. Let $E$ be an invertible module on $P\times_S Q$ [def-sc-invertible-module]. A $\mathbf G_m$-biextension structure on $E$ consists of trivializations of $E$ on the two identity axes which agree at the origin, and isomorphisms $E_{x+x',y}\simeq E_{x,y}\otimes E_{x',y}$ and $E_{x,y+y'}\simeq E_{x,y}\otimes E_{x,y'}$. Tensor product is [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product] and all modules at generalized points are tensor pullbacks [def-pc-module-pullback]. The isomorphisms are natural for arbitrary test schemes over $S$, hence are pulled back from their universal triple-product isomorphisms. Each law satisfies associativity, commutativity and the identity laws with the specified axis trivializations. Expanding $E_{x+x',y+y'}$ in either order gives the same morphism after the canonical permutation of the four tensor factors. An isomorphism of biextensions is an isomorphism of their underlying modules preserving both axis trivializations and both partial laws.

source.place: Revised March 14, 2021 thesis, Definition 3.2.1.1 and diagrams (3.2.1.2)--(3.2.1.6), printed pp.66--67; G_m-torsors realized by invertible modules. Read online at https://www.kwlan.org/articles/cpt-PEL-type-thesis-revision-dense.pdf.
